title: The gentleman of football: Andrés Escobar
post:
Andrés Escobar. Colombia's number two at USA 94. One touch against the hosts on 22 June 1994, and ten days later he was gone. Medellín still calls him the gentleman of football.

#andresescobar #colombia #worldcup #usa94 #football #footballhistory #medellin #footballtiktok

voice._name: Callum (ElevenLabs premade), eleven_v3 with audio tags in "say"; the settings of plea2005 (STYLE_BIBLE rule 68)

phrases.text: Andrés Escobar. Colombia's number two. One touch at the World Cup, and ten days later, he was gone.
phrases.say: [grave] Andrés Escobar. ... Colombia's number two. ... One touch at the World Cup... and ten days later... he was gone.

phrases.text: In 1994, Colombia came to the World Cup as one of the favourites. Months earlier, they had crushed Argentina 5–0 in Buenos Aires.
phrases.say: Nineteen ninety-four. Colombia came to the World Cup as one of the favourites. [building] Months earlier, they had crushed Argentina five–nil... in Buenos Aires.

phrases.text: But they lost their first game. Then, the hosts: the USA. A cross came in. Escobar stretched, and turned it into his own net. Colombia lost 2–1. Four days later, they were out.
phrases.say: But they lost their first game. ... Then, the hosts: the USA. [tense] A cross came in. Escobar stretched... and turned it into his own net. ... [quietly] Colombia lost two–one. Four days later, they were out.

phrases.text: He wrote in a newspaper: see you soon, because life doesn't end here.
phrases.say: [softly] He wrote in a newspaper: ... see you soon... because life doesn't end here.

phrases.text: On July 2, ten days after that match, he was shot dead outside a nightclub in Medellín. He was 27.
phrases.say: [grave] On July second... ten days after that match... he was shot dead outside a nightclub in Medellín. ... He was twenty-seven.

phrases.text: More than 100,000 people came to his funeral. Today his statue stands in Medellín, and they still call him the gentleman of football.
phrases.say: More than a hundred thousand people came to his funeral. ... [warmly] Today, his statue stands in Medellín... and they still call him... the gentleman of football.
